messages.subject: pearson residuals
parts:
Hi,

I used the examples of chapter 4 and 5 of 'The R-INLA tutorial: SPDE models'  by Krainski en Lindgren on my own data.
(slightly adapted the code)

r2 <- inla(y ~ 0 + z.b0 + y.b0 + f(i.z, model=spde) + f(i.y, copy='i.z', fixed=FALSE),
family=c('binomial', 'poisson'),
data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy), compute=TRUE))


This seems to work/run  

I do have a question: how can I calculate (pearson) residuals of  this model ? 
Are there options in the control.predictor or  is there a code example available somewhere ?


greetings 

Peter van Horssen

On Mon, 2013-11-25 at 07:59 -0800, peter van horssen wrote:


> I do have a question: how can I calculate (pearson) residuals of this
> model ?

we do not compute any 'residuals' now. in the Bayesian context, how do
we define residuals? would that be an distribution?

you can always use plugin estimates for the parameters (like the linear
predictor) and then get an estimate of the (pearson) residuals. (you
have to do that manually...)
